authority_journal.py.AuthoritySnapshot: Carry a verified authority sequence, state hash and decoded records, including transitions recovered from the witness; this is storage evidence, not a launch permit.
authority_journal.py.CommitReceipt: Identify a witnessed data transition and whether it was newly committed; receipt recovery does not repeat actor effects or grant execution.
authority_journal.py._History: Retain parsed witness progress, pending transition, replay receipts and a bounded incomplete-tail location for cross-store reconciliation.
authority_journal.py._canonical: Encode deterministic finite JSON bytes for this journal format; reject non-finite values instead of changing their meaning.
authority_journal.py._hash: Fingerprint the journal's canonical value representation for chain and state agreement checks.
authority_journal.py._unique: Reject duplicate JSON object keys so witness parsing cannot silently replace an earlier field.
authority_journal.py._decode: Decode journal JSON while rejecting duplicate keys and non-finite numeric constants.
authority_journal.py._nonfinite: Reject an unsupported JSON numeric constant rather than admitting a non-finite authority value.
authority_journal.py._sequence: Recognize a nonnegative signed-64-bit journal sequence, excluding boolean lookalikes.
authority_journal.py._state_digest: Recognize the exact lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 representation required by the journal format.
authority_journal.py._key: Validate a nonempty printable authority record key within the format's character bound.
authority_journal.py._operation_id: Validate a replayable transition identity while reserving genesis for externally provisioned history.
authority_journal.py._delta: Validate disjoint bounded record updates/deletions and detach mutable caller values by canonical serialization before any write.
authority_journal.py._apply: Produce a new bounded authority record set from a delta without mutating the supplied mapping.
authority_journal.py._envelope: Bind a witness payload to the preceding chain digest and compute its record fingerprint.
authority_journal.py._intent: Fingerprint a transition's original predecessor and record delta, independently of later commit metadata.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal.__enter__: Use the already opened journal in a context; missing authority is never initialized by context entry.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal.__exit__: Release this journal's file handles without treating context exit as actor closure or rollback of an already witnessed transition.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal._identity: Represent the physical device/inode pair used to detect replacement of an opened authority file.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal._check_files: Reject inherited, closed, replaced or unsafe original files and enforce the provisioned database capacity before further journal operations.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal._operation: Serialize local access and take a nonblocking cross-process lock over revalidated authority handles; roll back any transaction left open by the operation.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal._connection: Open the existing authority database with zero lock wait and required DELETE/EXTRA durability settings; never create or migrate its format.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal._state: Validate bounded canonical SQL rows against their recorded state hash and authority identity; agreement with the external witness is checked separately.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal._prepare: Validate the exact PREPARE fields, canonical delta and immediate committed predecessor without applying the transition.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal._append_record: Append and fsync one bounded witness record linked to the previous digest, retaining history when capacity is exhausted.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal._sync_database: Fsync the original database and its parent directory after authority state changes.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal._write_databas: Apply the already witnessed delta, verify the resulting state hash, commit SQL and synchronize its durable files.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal._verified: Reconcile SQL and witness forward through a durable PREPARE, trimming only a mutually validated torn tail; never replay actor execution or accept a rewind.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal.load: Return verified authority state, potentially completing witnessed storage recovery; loading is not a read-only operation or an execution authorization.
authority_journal.py.WitnessedAuthorityJournal.commit: Compare the original expected state and commit one bounded witnessed delta; the same transition ID recovers its original receipt, while changed intent conflicts.

codex_rpc.py.RpcReply: Pair a matched RPC result with the count of preceding public wire messages so consumers can account for streamed events before accepting the result.
codex_rpc.py.RpcError.__init__: Preserve the peer's explicit error code and message as a failed response rather than a successful result.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient.__init__: Configure bounded requests, frames and event queues around a lifecycle-owned endpoint; construction starts no process or protocol reader.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient._serve_private: Serve one separately registered host control request under its current guard and deadline, sanitizing callback failures before closing the connection.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient.__aenter__: Open the endpoint exactly once and start frame/stderr consumers; failed or cancelled startup drains owned endpoint cleanup.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient.__aexit__: Await the shared owned connection shutdown when the async scope exits.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient.request: Send one correlated request and return its matched result, discarding only the event barrier metadata; a lost response is never replayed automatically.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient.notify: Write a notification without registering a response future; successful writing is not peer acknowledgement or effect completion.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient.respond: Reply to the peer's original request identity, optionally rechecking private control authority at the write boundary.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient._check_connection: Expose the first permanent transport failure or reject use before startup; this check does not reconnect.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient._send: Serialize one bounded finite JSON frame under the write lock and recheck any private guard immediately before writing.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient._fail: Retain the first connection failure and wake pending request and event observers without synthesizing successful receipts.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient._read_messages: Parse bounded frames, correlate only matching live reply IDs and route private controls separately from queued events; malformed or overloaded input ends the connection.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient._drain_stderr: Consume peer diagnostic bytes until EOF without retaining or logging them through this transport.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient._begin_close: Create or recover one shared endpoint shutdown task so concurrent close requests cannot start competing teardown paths.
codex_rpc.py.JsonRpcClient._shutdown: Fail pending RPC observers, close the owned endpoint and drain reader/private-control tasks even when endpoint teardown raises.
codex_rpc.py._SubprocessEndpoint.__init__: Retain a compatibility subprocess invocation and environment copy without spawning or claiming broker containment.
codex_rpc.py._SubprocessEndpoint.open: Start one subprocess session with piped transport and a bounded reader; shield creation so the owner can later drain a cancelled startup.
codex_rpc.py._SubprocessEndpoint._signal: Signal the configured original process or process group, tolerating an already missing process without claiming namespace retirement.
codex_rpc.py._SubprocessEndpoint.aclose: Close input and reap the started compatibility child with TERM/KILL escalation; process-group signaling is not the broker's registered-domain proof.
codex_rpc.py.StdioRpcClient.__init__: Configure the CLI compatibility endpoint and bounded JSON-RPC client without starting a child or selecting subscription credentials.
codex_rpc.py.StdioRpcClient.command.getter: Return the invocation vector retained by the compatibility endpoint; reading it does not dispatch a command.
codex_rpc.py.StdioRpcClient.command.setter: Replace the endpoint's configured invocation vector without restarting an existing connection.
codex_rpc.py.StdioRpcClient.cwd.getter: Return the directory option configured for compatibility process creation.
codex_rpc.py.StdioRpcClient.cwd.setter: Replace the endpoint directory option without moving a process that is already running.
codex_rpc.py.StdioRpcClient.env.getter: Return the configured environment mapping; None retains the subprocess API's parent-environment inheritance behavior.
codex_rpc.py.StdioRpcClient.env.setter: Replace the environment passed to future endpoint creation; this compatibility property does not filter credentials or validate its contents.
codex_rpc.py.StdioRpcClient.process_group_signals.get: Report whether compatibility teardown signals a process group rather than only its direct child.
codex_rpc.py.StdioRpcClient.process_group_signals.set: Set compatibility signaling mode without registering or proving closure of a broker-owned namespace.

command_jobs.py._Command: Retain one reserved command's bounded output buffers, execution/cancellation tasks and response barrier on its original connection.
command_jobs.py.CommandHandle: Observe or cancel one existing command through its original executor; the handle does not grant another dispatch.
command_jobs.py.CommandHandle.__init__: Bind a lightweight handle to the original executor and durable job identity without launching work.
command_jobs.py.CommandHandle.wait: Shield the existing local execution task from observer cancellation, then read the original durable receipt instead of restarting it.
command_jobs.py.CommandHandle.cancel: Request cancellation through the original executor and return the resulting retained receipt.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor: Own one account-free command peer and its original-attempt receipts, separating streamed output, cancellation intent and physical peer closure.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor.__init__: Bind journal, workspace and lease only to their own registered command transport; connection and account checks occur on async entry.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor.__aenter__: Initialize the dedicated RPC peer, reject an attached account and require its bound identity before starting event and authority monitors.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor.__aexit__: Await the executor's shared cancellation and peer teardown when its scope exits.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor.start: Reserve one scoped command before its first dispatch, or recover its original handle/receipt; an uncertain command from another connection requires reconciliation.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._get: Read a retained command only within this executor's admitted run, independently of whether that command may still execute.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._read_events: Consume command-only notifications and advance the reply barrier; unexpected interactive requests or malformed transport trigger peer retirement.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._output: Append decoded bytes only to the matching active command up to its stream limit, requesting cancellation when capture reaches its bound.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._barrier: Wait for the event consumer to process every public wire message preceding a command reply, exposing reader failures or the bounded wait timeout.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._execute: Dispatch the reserved command once, account for preceding output and persist its recognized terminal observation; transport failure closes the peer and retains an unknown exit.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._watch_owner: Supervise durable attempt authority and stop active command effects when authority is absent or cannot be established.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._ensure_cancel: Create or recover one cancellation task for this command without repeating execution.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor.cancel: Share cancellation for a locally tracked command or inspect an older retained receipt without acquiring a new execution owner.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._cancel: Record cancellation intent and retry only termination control within grace, then cross the physical peer closure barrier before collecting the original command outcome.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor.aclose: Await one shared executor shutdown while shielding it from cancellation of an observer.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._shutdown: Request cancellation of active jobs, always close the peer and drain the event reader; peer teardown errors remain visible.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._close_peer: Create or recover one shielded retirement task for the executor's original peer.
command_jobs.py.OwnedCommandExecutor._retire_peer: Use broker-owned closure when available; otherwise drain RPC and registered namespace closure together and propagate unresolved teardown errors.

execution_domain.py._deadline: Validate a finite positive timeout of at most 60seconds and return its absolute monotonic deadline.
execution_domain.py.DomainIdentity: Pin an opened cgroup object together with boot, observer and cgroup-namespace identities; this value is not an execution grant.
execution_domain.py.ContainedChild.__init__: Own the child's pidfd and unbuffered transport pipes for later observation and reaping, without certifying subtree closure.
execution_domain.py.ContainedChild.wait: Poll the owned pidfd and cache the reaped direct-child exit; timeout or external reaping does not become an invented terminal receipt.
execution_domain.py.ContainedChild.close_handles: Release transport streams and the pidfd without terminating or certifying retirement of the execution domain.
execution_domain.py.ExecutionDomain.open: Open an existing non-threaded cgroup domain, reject the controller's ancestry and optionally match an externally retained identity; never provision a new domain.
execution_domain.py.ExecutionDomain.__enter__: Use the already opened domain without starting or releasing an actor.
execution_domain.py.ExecutionDomain.__exit__: Release domain handles on context exit; actor retirement remains a separate explicit operation.
execution_domain.py.ExecutionDomain.close: Release local directory descriptors, including inherited handles after fork, without killing actors or claiming the domain is empty.
execution_domain.py.ExecutionDomain._reject_own_ancestors: Reject a domain containing the controller or one of its ancestors before the object can be used for subtree retirement.
execution_domain.py.ExecutionDomain._check: Require the same live opened object, process, boot and observer namespaces; replaced or retired paths require explicit reconciliation.
execution_domain.py.ExecutionDomain._read: Read one bounded ASCII control-file window relative to the pinned domain descriptor without following a symlink leaf.
execution_domain.py.ExecutionDomain._kill: Signal cgroup.kill through a duplicated, identity-checked subtree handle; the caller must separately establish emptiness and removal.
